limitation: The data is daily; there is no hourly or opening-time information.
effect_on_conclusions: Opening and closing behaviour can only be studied as open vs closed days.

limitation: Promotion effects are observed associations, not controlled experiments.
effect_on_conclusions: No causal uplift can be claimed; Promo2 stores selling less may reflect who is targeted.

limitation: Only daily customer counts exist.
effect_on_conclusions: Returning vs new customers cannot be identified.

limitation: There is no location information (no city or city-centre flag).
effect_on_conclusions: The city-centre part of the competitor-distance question cannot be tested.

limitation: store.csv is a static snapshot.
effect_on_conclusions: Changes from missing to known competitor distance over time cannot be observed.

limitation: test.csv has no Sales or Customers.
effect_on_conclusions: Accuracy can only be measured on labelled history, not on the supplied test period.

limitation: 180 stores are missing the same six-month block in one year.
effect_on_conclusions: Needs flagging; rolling and sequence features must not cross the gap.

limitation: School holidays are far more common in test (44%) than in train (18%); state holidays b and c never occur in test.
effect_on_conclusions: Train/test shift: performance on those patterns cannot be confirmed from the test period.

limitation: The cause of the shared six-month missing block is not in the data (planned closure, refurbishment or missing data).
effect_on_conclusions: Forecasts for these stores rely on history on either side of the block; features must not cross it.

limitation: The cause of the 54 open zero-sales days cannot be confirmed.
effect_on_conclusions: They are excluded from training on the evidence of their pattern, not on a confirmed explanation.

limitation: Three competitors open after the last training date, inside the forecast window.
effect_on_conclusions: Their effect on those stores cannot be learned from training history.

limitation: About one third of stores have no usable competitor opening date.
effect_on_conclusions: Competition-age features carry an 'unknown' group, which weakens conclusions about competitor openings.

limitation: Store 622's 11 missing Open values in test are assumed open from a rule, not from supplied plans.
effect_on_conclusions: If the store is actually closed on those days, its forecasts for them are overstated.

limitation: Validation uses actual Open, Promo and holiday values as if they were known plans.
effect_on_conclusions: If real plans change after the forecast is made, true errors will be somewhat larger than validation suggests.

limitation: The rolling windows (February to June) contain little of the summer school-holiday pattern (4% to 23% of days against 44% in test).
effect_on_conclusions: Only the seasonal check resembles the test window, and it has fewer stores and a shorter training history.

limitation: The 42-day holdout does not cover forecast days 43 to 48 of the 48-day test window.
effect_on_conclusions: Those days are checked only through the seasonal check.

limitation: Only about two and a half years of history exist, with one complete earlier summer (2013) and a partial 2014 summer for 180 stores.
effect_on_conclusions: Summer seasonality is learned from very few examples.

limitation: A single 42-day holdout is one draw of forecast conditions.
effect_on_conclusions: Holdout error has sampling noise; conclusions rely on the holdout, rolling windows and seasonal check together.

limitation: All stores share one promotion calendar, so promotion effects come from timing (alternating weeks) and are not experimental.
effect_on_conclusions: Lift figures are associations; they could partly reflect other weekly patterns.

limitation: Customers cannot be split into existing and new customers.
effect_on_conclusions: The effect of promotions on existing customers is only visible indirectly (customers, spend per customer, following days).

limitation: Holiday effects rest on 3 Easters, 2 Christmases and 14 national holidays; regional holidays were not analysed.
effect_on_conclusions: Holiday uplifts are averages over very few events.

limitation: Competitor-opening analysis covers 120 stores with complete history and a known opening month; dates are accurate only to the month.
effect_on_conclusions: The size of the effect is approximate and may differ for stores excluded from the analysis.

limitation: Sunday trading is rare (33 stores) and tied to store type; only 13 type a stores allow a like-with-like comparison.
effect_on_conclusions: The Sunday-trading findings are tentative.

limitation: The exploration excludes the final 42 days, so the most recent weeks are not shown.
effect_on_conclusions: Patterns in the last weeks before the test window are not described here.

limitation: Same-year-earlier features are missing for the first year of training rows (2013) and for the 180 stores with the 2014 gap in the test window.
effect_on_conclusions: Models must handle missing values; forecasts for those stores rely on recent history instead.

limitation: Holiday distances rely on holidays that appear in the files. Regional events that are not flagged (for example 16 February 2015) cause large errors on those days.
effect_on_conclusions: Some of the hardest days to forecast are regional events the data does not mark.

limitation: The same target day can appear in up to two forecast origins, with different horizons and history.
effect_on_conclusions: Training rows are not independent; validation stays leak-free because each window uses one origin.

limitation: Sunday and holiday forecasts for the 33 stores that trade on Sundays are the hardest, with few examples.
effect_on_conclusions: Errors on those days (RMSPE up to 0.9) can dominate a window's score.

limitation: The comparison of feature sets used one fast model on a 300,000-row sample.
effect_on_conclusions: The size of the improvement is indicative; Section 7 repeats it with the final models.

limitation: Tuning used 100,000-row samples and small searches (4, 3 and 6 configurations), and the comparison used 150,000 training rows.
effect_on_conclusions: Settings may not be optimal and the reported errors are higher than a full-data fit will give.

limitation: State holidays (RMSPE 0.64) and the few stores that trade on Sundays (0.34) are forecast poorly, on very few rows.
effect_on_conclusions: A handful of holiday and Sunday days dominate a window's score; typical weekdays are around 0.10 to 0.12.

limitation: Week-by-week error depends on what the window contains: in the rolling windows week 1 is hardest because holidays fall early, while in the holiday-free seasonal check the error rises from 0.09 to 0.12 over four weeks.
effect_on_conclusions: Forecast quality for weeks 3 to 6 of the real test window should be expected to sit between these patterns.

limitation: The finalist forecasts about 1% too low on average and is least accurate on promotion days in the rolling windows (0.152 against 0.116).
effect_on_conclusions: Totals can be slightly understated; promotion-day forecasts deserve attention in the final model.

limitation: The registered models were trained on samples of the rolling window 3 training rows, not on all history.
effect_on_conclusions: They are candidates for comparison, not the final deliverable.

limitation: The chain average on Sundays is the average of the few stores that trade on Sundays (about 27 on a typical Sunday), which are large type b stores.
effect_on_conclusions: Sundays look unusually strong at chain level; this is a mix effect, not a pattern of all stores.

limitation: Stationarity tests describe the aggregate over only 2.5 years; the yearly cycle cannot be tested (a one-year lag has only 536 pairs) and holidays create outliers.
effect_on_conclusions: Conclusions about trend and yearly seasonality are tentative.

limitation: Individual stores differ: two of the four typical stores (types a and c) are level-stationary, while the type b and type d stores are only trend-stationary.
effect_on_conclusions: A single transformation rule may not suit every store; a shared model needs store-level scaling.

limitation: The store LSTM was trained on a CPU budget (40,960 samples per epoch, at most 8 epochs; 8 epochs on average before early stopping).
effect_on_conclusions: A GPU and a larger budget could lower its error; the comparison is fair for the stated budget, not a ceiling for LSTMs.

limitation: LSTM results vary with the seed (store LSTM, rolling 3: standard deviation 0.0067 over 3 seeds; chain variants: Table of seed standard deviations).
effect_on_conclusions: Differences between LSTM variants smaller than the seed spread are not meaningful.

limitation: The chain-level LSTM forecasts one aggregate series (about 100 training origins per split), not store-day sales.
effect_on_conclusions: It shows the brief's time-series steps on the series of 8.1; store forecasts come from the shared store model.
